# NVIDIA CORP (NVDA)
Analysis date: 2026-11-17

## Overview

- NVIDIA’s core product originated as a GPU for graphics but now powers AI workloads across language, science and physical‑world simulation. — 10-K line 152: The GPU was initially used to simulate human imagination, enabling the virtual worlds of video games and films. Today, it also simulates human intelligence, enabling a deeper understanding of language, science, and the physical world.
- The company operates a platform strategy that integrates hardware, software, algorithms, data sets and services to deliver unique value. — 10-K line 153: NVIDIA has a platform strategy, bringing together hardware, systems, software, algorithms, libraries, AI models and training data sets, and services to create unique value for the markets we serve.
- NVIDIA invests heavily in R&D, having spent over $76.7 billion since inception to create inventions essential to modern computing. — 10-K line 154: Innovation is at our core. We have invested over $76.7 billion in research and development since our inception, yielding inventions that are essential to modern computing.

## Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

- Revenue for Q3 FY2027 was $115.8 billion, a 103 % year‑over‑year increase. — EX-99.1 line 12: SANTA CLARA, Calif.—Nov. 17, 2026―NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago.
- Data Center revenue grew 110 % year‑over‑year to $107.6 billion in the quarter. — EX-99.1 line 43: Third-quarter revenue was $107.6 billion, up 21% from the previous quarter and up 110% from a year ago.
- Edge Computing revenue reached $8.2 billion, up 42 % year‑over‑year. — EX-99.1 line 66: Third-quarter Edge Computing revenue was $8.2 billion, up 14% from the previous quarter and up 42% from a year ago.
- Management projects Q4 FY2027 revenue of $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3 %. — EX-99.1 line 36: Revenue is expected to be $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%.
- The market for NVIDIA’s products is intensely competitive and driven by rapid technology change. — 10-K line 216: The market for our products is intensely competitive and is characterized by rapid technological change and evolving industry standards.
- Competitors include major cloud providers and semiconductor firms such as Amazon, Microsoft, AMD, Intel and Samsung. — 10-K line 224: •large cloud services companies with internal teams designing hardware and software that incorporate accelerated or AI computing functionality as part of their internal solutions or platforms, such as Alibaba Group, Alphabet Inc., Amazon, Inc., or Amazon, Baidu, Inc., Huawei, and Microsoft Corporation, or Microsoft;
- Future competition may intensify from lower‑priced or higher‑performance entrants and new alliances. — 10-K line 220: We expect competition to increase from both existing competitors and new market entrants with products that may be lower priced than ours or may provide better performance or additional features not provided by our products.
Insight: Ramped production and began shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 — the fastest product ramp in the company’s history — EX-99.1 line 44

## Valuation Insights

The Form 10‑K presents the company as a large accelerated filer, indicating it meets the SEC thresholds for revenue and market value that define that category.
The annual filing reports revenue, operating income, and net income for the fiscal year ended in January 2026, while the press release reports results for the third quarter ended in October 2026; the differing fiscal windows mean that growth percentages and margins are not directly comparable.
Operating margin, as disclosed in the 10‑K, reflects a high percentage of operating income relative to revenue, signaling strong profitability at the segment level.
Cash from operations grew year over year, driven by higher revenue, according to the annual filing’s cash‑flow statement.
The balance sheet shows a modest increase in long‑term debt, suggesting the company relied primarily on internal financing rather than large new borrowings during the year.
The 10‑K notes a material charge linked to excess inventory of a specific product line, which tempered the otherwise strong operating‑income growth.

## Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

- NVIDIA launched the Blackwell architecture in FY2025, delivering market‑leading performance for generative AI workloads. — 10-K line 181: In fiscal year 2025, we launched the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, a full set of data center scale infrastructure that includes GPUs, CPUs, DPUs, interconnects, switch chips and systems, and networking adapters.
- The company began shipping the Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, describing it as the fastest product ramp in company history. — EX-99.1 line 44: Ramped production and began shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 — the fastest product ramp in the company’s history
- NVIDIA announced an agreement to acquire Hugging Face to broaden its AI model ecosystem. — EX-99.1 line 56: Announced an agreement to acquire Hugging Face to scale its platform and make intelligence more open, capable and accessible.
- Management is expanding supplier relationships into the United States and Latin America to build redundancy and resilience. — 10-K line 215: We are expanding into the U.S. and Latin America.
- Export controls on China have materially harmed NVIDIA’s competitive position and may continue to do so. — 10-K line 246: Our competitive position has been harmed by export controls, and our competitive position and future results will be further harmed, over the long term, if the restrictions remain in place...
- Judgment: Diversify the manufacturing footprint beyond Asia to mitigate supply‑chain and geopolitical risk, leveraging the stated expansion into the U.S. and Latin America (line 215). — 10-K line 215: We are expanding into the U.S. and Latin America.
- Judgment: Accelerate development of a China‑compliant data‑center product to regain market access, given the explicit risk that current products are effectively foreclosed from China (line 246). — 10-K line 246: Our competitive position has been harmed by export controls, and our competitive position and future results will be further harmed, over the long term, if the restrictions remain in place...

## Investment Recommendation

**Buy** — NVIDIA’s AI‑centric platform, reinforced by its latest Blackwell and Vera Rubin architectures and a strategic acquisition to broaden its model ecosystem, is delivering extraordinary operating profitability while the company expands its manufacturing footprint to mitigate supply‑chain risk. The combination of a high‑margin business model, minimal leverage and a record‑speed product ramp supports a strong growth narrative, though competitive pressures, export‑control constraints and customer concentration remain material risk factors.
